response.title: Reading the River
response.passage:
On a warm Saturday in July, the Green Club met beside a river that ran through the town park. Heavy rain had washed plastic cups and branches onto the bank, and the mess was beginning to bother visitors. The club had only a few pairs of gloves and one coil of rope. Its members first thought they could finish the cleanup by themselves. The students agreed to cooperate with the park staff, since neither group could clear the bank alone. That decision gave them enough people to divide the work safely.

Before anyone entered the shallow water, Ms. Lin asked the group to study the river from the path. A map showed that the stream bent sharply near a footbridge, and one student guessed that the turn might explain why so much litter had collected there. To check that guess, two students chose to observe the water for ten minutes and mark where floating leaves slowed down. Their notes showed that leaves gathered just below the bend, where the bank was wide and easy to reach. The team decided to begin there instead of spreading out along the whole river.

Near the footbridge, a volunteer noticed that the rope in their kit had a frayed section. Ms. Lin went to the park shed and brought back a reliable rope that she had checked earlier that morning. With that secure line in place, the students could pull larger branches toward the bank without stepping into deeper water. They filled several bags with cups and wrappers, while the staff moved heavy branches out of the walking path. No one rushed, and the group paused whenever a task required more hands.

By midday, the bank looked much cleaner, but a few bottles remained caught among the reeds. A strong current kept pushing them farther downstream whenever someone reached toward them from the shore. The team left those bottles alone and reported their location to the park workers, who had a long-handled tool for the job. Before leaving, the students checked the path for loose gloves and thanked the staff for their help. The club planned to return after the next heavy rain, now knowing where litter was most likely to collect.
